newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka forces step up airstrikes on Tamil rebels.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka forces step up airstrikes on Tamil rebels.

text.p: Sri Lankan air force planes blew up three vehicles bringing up Tamil Tiger rebel reinforcements trying to halt an army advance on Saturday, military officials said.

"The air force destroyed three heavy vehicles with reinforcements on the Nedunkeni-Oddusuddan road," a military official said. "Enemy casualties are not immediately known but are believed to be heavy."
The air attack was on the eastern flank of a three-pronged army thrust into territory held by Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels in the northern mainland Wanni region.
A military spokesman said earlier the security forces used artillery and helicopter gunships to attack rebel reinforcements trying to stall the army's advance.
"We have engaged the enemy with artillery and Mi-24 helicopters in the area east of Omanthai," he told Reuters. "About 300 terrorists were in the area and they have suffered heavy casualties."

The Defence Ministry says the main aim of the drive was to capture areas in the shrub-covered Wanni from the LTTE, who are waging a war for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in predominantly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.

A pitched battle was fought near Nedunkeni, about 40 km (25 miles) northeast of Vavuniya, where troops advancing along the eastern flank were attacked by the rebels on Friday, military officials said.
The troops earlier beat off an overnight counter-attack by Tamil Tiger rebels to consolidate their hold on the town of Omanthai, 14 km (nine miles) north of Vavuniya, military officials said.
Both sides have exchanged heavy artillery and mortar fire during the last two days of the fighting, the officials said.
They said troops were now pushing north, heading towards the heavily fortified rebel-held town of Puliyankulam.
Military officials said some 40 soldiers and more than 128 rebels had been killed in the fighting so far.
Hospital officials said some 320 soldiers wounded in the past two days of fighting had been sent to hospitals in northern Anuradhapura and Jaffna and in Colombo.

The military has been tight-lipped about where the troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air cover, are heading after breaking out of Vavuniya to launch the offensive code-named "Jaya Sikuru," or "Sure of Victory" five days ago.
Analysts said the offensive aims to open a land supply route linking Vavuniya, 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, with Jaffna peninsula, about 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The LTTE has, however, accused the military of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property in the guise of opening a supply route.
The LTTE said in a statement on Saturday that air force planes dropped incendiary bombs setting on fire a jungle near Puliyankulam.
"Communities of Tamil people living in the forest are in panic," it said.
Journalists have not yet been allowed into the battle zone.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
